ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35), as amended; Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (Public Act 2013 No 69); and the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2023, requiring an ultimate beneficial ownership register at the New Zealand Companies Office accessible to competent authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Non-Dissolution and Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: New Zealand issuing path: certificate to be extracted from the companies register and digitally signed by the Registrar; for use in an Apostille Convention country, the original paper copy is certified by the Department of Internal Affairs' Authentications Unit with a Hague Apostille. For use in a non-member country, the certificate is first notarized by a New Zealand notary public and then legalized by the consulate of the destination country in New Zealand. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation and appointing local director/compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate beneficial owner or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board resolution and power of attorney must be executed before a notary public in the jurisdiction of execution. In an Apostille Convention state, the notary's certificate is then submitted to the designated Competent Authority for apostille (e.g., the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs if executed in NZ). In a non-member state, the notarized document must be legalized by the destination country's embassy or consulate accredited to the state of execution. Only one of the two authentication paths may be used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate parent or shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies in the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, ACRA, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication depends on the country of issue. If the issuing registry is in an Apostille contracting state, the registry certificate is apostilled by that state's central authority and accepted in New Zealand without further legalization. If the issuing registry is in a non-contracting state, the certificate must be notarized and then legalized by the New Zealand High Commission or Consulate having jurisdiction. The two methods are exclusive and non-chainable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitution of the proposed New Zealand limited company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders and incorporating agent; to be registered with the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Because the proposed New Zealand company will be registered domestically, the constitution does not require foreign authentication. Upon incorporation, the Companies Office will issue a certified extract of the constitution; for overseas use in Apostille states, a Hague Apostille from the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs is required; for overseas use in non-member states, consular legalization by the destination state's New Zealand consulate is required instead. Do not apply both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (bank capacity, history, and relationship integrity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or relationship bank of the ultimate beneficial owner or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be on original bank letterhead, signed by a compliance officer, and notarized. If the bank is domiciled in an Apostille state, obtain an apostille from the appropriate national authority (e.g., in New Zealand, Department of Internal Affairs). If not, have the notarized letter legalized by the relevant New Zealand consulate. These are alternative paths and cannot be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, and proposed compliance officers against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, the Australian Consolidated List, and New Zealand's Designated Terrorist Entities List and asset freeze notices issued under the Sanctions Act 1979, the Russia Sanctions Act 2022, and the AML/CFT Act 2009. Enhanced due diligence requires open-source and commercial database checks, adverse media screening, and documentation of control enhancements for any politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign and domestic PEPs, their immediate family members and close associates. All screening results must be documented in an AML/CFT compliance file and refreshed every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online portal (Companies Register), specifically the Name Availability Search and Reserve a Name application service at companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Companies Act 1993 and Companies (Name) Regulations 2006, a company name must be in Roman script, may contain macrons when using Māori language terms, and must not include any symbol other than permitted punctuation. Where a foreign-language name is used, a phonetic transliteration in Latin characters must be provided to ensure the name is searchable and not confusingly similar to existing names. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) the name must be unique; (2) it must not be reserved by another applicant; (3) it must not be contrary to New Zealand law or contain restricted words without approval; and (4) it must be capable of distinguishing the company from others.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must first file a written request for statement of reasons within 10 working days of the notice. After receiving reasons, the applicant may submit a formal application for internal review to the Registrar of Companies, attaching evidence of distinctiveness or prior ministerial approval. The review process must be initiated within 20 working days from the date of the rejection notice. If internal review confirms refusal, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993 within 20 working days. A fee applies for each stage. The appeal is a full rehearing, and the burden is on the applicant to show the name is not offensive or misleading and is otherwise available for registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a licensed legal-service entity (ISIC 6910) in New Zealand, a bare virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office. Inland Revenue requires a physical business address for GST and income tax registration, and the New Zealand Law Society's trust-account rules require a physical office where client trust funds are administered. Banks conducting AML/CFT customer due diligence will generally decline an application if the entity uses only a virtual office or shared mailbox for a law practice. A managed physical office with an active presence, separate meeting space, and named responsible person is permitted, but must be disclosed and approved by the Law Society.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified likelihood: Moderate, approximately 35% in any 12-month period for a licensed litigation firm. Checklist: (1) IRD may conduct unannounced visits to verify the registered office is not a PO box; (2) the Companies Office may audit for maintaining an open-to-public registered office during working hours; (3) the New Zealand Law Society conducts periodic practice inspections, including unannounced trust-account audits; (4) local territorial authority may inspect zoning and business signage if the office is in a commercial building; (5) banks may perform site visits as part of enhanced due diligence. Maintain staff at the physical location and retain lease and utility records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 11-21, 51-58, 81-91, 120-153, 161-166; Companies Regulations 1994; Financial Reporting Act 2013; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a functional authority within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Company; company constitution (if adopted); consent to act as director; company name reservation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account rule. A company must issue at least one share to one shareholder, and shares may be issued fully or partly paid for cash, property, or other lawful consideration. The directors must record subscription consideration in the share register and ensure that all allotments comply with section 54 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS IN WRITING OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED, adopted pursuant to section 91 of the Companies Act 1993. The undersigned director(s), constituting the duly appointed board, hereby resolve as follows. 1. RATIFICATION OF INCORPORATION: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 1993, its Constitution, and the particulars registered with the Companies Office be and is hereby ratified, confirmed, and adopted; and that all lawful acts done by the directors and subscribers before this date in connection with the formation of the Company are hereby ratified and approved. 2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: RESOLVED that the initial share capital of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [●] ordinary shares, and that such shares be allotted to the subscribers named in the share register upon payment or liability to pay the agreed subscription consideration, which consideration is hereby acknowledged as fully credited in accordance with sections 52 to 54 of the Companies Act 1993; RESOLVED FURTHER that the board is authorized to determine the issue price, class rights, dividend rights, voting rights, and transfer restrictions of any subsequent share issues, to maintain the share register, and to issue share certificates in the prescribed form. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [registered office address], New Zealand, being the address accepted by the Registrar for the service of legal process and statutory notices; and that any future change of registered office be made by filing the prescribed notice with the Companies Office and giving concurrent written notice to the Inland Revenue Department and the New Zealand Law Society if the Company remains an incorporated legal practice. 4. BANKING AND TRUST ACCOUNT: RESOLVED that [bank name] be and is hereby appointed as the principal banker of the Company; that the directors and named officers be and are hereby authorized to open operating accounts, foreign currency accounts, IOLTA-compliant client trust accounts, and term deposit facilities; that any two authorized signatories acting together, or the sole director acting alone if so mandated, sign cheques, electronic instructions, loan documents, guarantees, indemnities

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand, with secure online portal myIR at www.ird.govt.nz; export and customs clearance is administered by New Zealand Customs Service (Te Mana Arai o Aotearoa) through the Trade Single Window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident corporate entity (an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993): (1) determine whether the entity is carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand, has New Zealand source income, or will make taxable supplies in New Zealand; (2) if it establishes a place of business or commences a taxable activity, register the overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office and obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); (3) apply for the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number using the prescribed non-resident company application form (IR742), either by paper application or through an authorised New Zealand tax agent lodging via myIR; (4) provide certified entity formation documents, certificate of incorporation, global register of directors and shareholders, registered office information, and details of the intended New Zealand business operations; (5) if annual taxable supplies will exceed the Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration threshold, complete the GST registration election as part of the same IRD number registration or later through myIR; (6) the same IRD number serves as the income tax TIN and the GST/VAT registration identifier; no separate VAT ID exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a New Zealand limited company (Ltd) is a separate taxable entity resident in New Zealand; it is subject to New Zealand corporate income tax on worldwide income under the Income Tax Act 2007, with the New Zealand full imputation regime applying to shareholder distributions. No subnational income tax applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (no US-style check-the-box regime). Statutory elections available under New Zealand law include: (a) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Tax Administration Act 1994, making an eligible close-held company transparent for income tax purposes; (b) imputation company election to establish and maintain an imputation credit account; (c) hybrid mismatch rules under subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 are mandatory anti-avoidance provisions, not elective classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (New Zealand GST/VAT system)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; registration is compulsory once the threshold is exceeded or is expected to be exceeded, including for non-resident suppliers of remote or digital services supplied to New Zealand consumers under the remote services GST regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-clearance API, or anti-fraud digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. Inland Revenue accepts electronic records and GST returns filed through myIR; voluntary e-Invoicing is supported through the PEPPOL-based e-Invoicing network administered by the New Zealand Electronic Invoicing Board and promoted for business-to-government transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a supply is zero-rated where the supplier exports goods from New Zealand within the statutory time frame (generally 28 days after the time of supply), or supplies services such as cross-border commercial arbitration, legal advice, and asset-tracing services to a non-resident client who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and who does not receive the services directly in connection with New Zealand land or goods physically located in New Zealand; qualifying remote and digital services supplied to non-resident customers may also be zero-rated. The supplier must hold adequate documentary proof of export and of the customer's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Entry (customs export declaration) lodged through New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window, together with the approved customs clearance record
Ocean Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill or Air Waybill / Air Cargo Manifest evidencing physical export from New Zealand and the overseas destination
Commercial invoice, service agreement, or professional engagement letter identifying the non-resident client and describing the cross-border legal, arbitration, or asset-tracing services
Bank or SWIFT payment transfer advice evidencing foreign-currency consideration, accepted as substantiation of the export or service proceeds
Evidence of non-residency of the customer, such as a tax residence certificate, passport, registered office record, or statutory declaration, and, for goods, packing list and inventory records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand has no foreign-exchange control regime and no statutory FX repatriation deadline or Inward Remittance Certificate requirement. However, export zero-rating is audited by Inland Revenue using myIR data, New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window records, and bank/payment-rail information. If export zero-rating is not substantiated, the supply is re-assessed as taxable GST at 15%, with use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: up to 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. The Commissioner of Inland Revenue may revisit returns generally within 4 years, or within 10 years in cases of fraud or evasion, and records supporting zero-rated exports must be retained for 7 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised foreign exchange regime. The New Zealand dollar is freely convertible for both current-account items such as legal retainers, expert witness fees, dividends, interest, and trade payments, and for capital-account items such as equity injections, intercompany loans, and asset acquisitions. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not require exchange surrender, prior approval, or a foreign-exchange licence for ordinary commercial transactions. Profit remittance from a New Zealand Limited company is not subject to FX conversion limits; however, non-resident withholding tax and double-tax-agreement documentation will apply to dividends and interest, and the bank will require standard tax declarations. Large international transfers are captured by the AML/CFT Act 2009 and by RBNZ balance-of-payments statistical reporting, but these do not operate as controls on convertibility. The only material inbound investment screen is the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which is relevant only for sensitive land or significant business assets; a litigation chambers company holding no sensitive New Zealand assets will fall outside that screening threshold. Overall, capital and current account convertibility are unrestricted, the NZD market is deep and liquid, and regulated hedging is available onshore.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Foreign currency receipts may be retained in domestic or offshore foreign-currency accounts, converted at negotiated commercial rates, or used as the documented underlying exposure for bank-provided FX hedges. Only balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligations apply to the resident receiving bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Solicitors' Trust Account (IOLTA-style) / NZD and Foreign Currency Operating Account
Client Trust Account / Business Transaction Account and Capital Escrow Account
Solicitors' Trust Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Trust and Escrow Account / Cross-Border Settlement and FX Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. New Zealand's solicitors' trust account regime requires client funds to be held with a New Zealand registered bank or an entity expressly authorised under the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 and relevant trust account regulations. Offshore fintech EMIs are not registered banks in New Zealand and cannot legally serve as the depository for IOLTA-style client trust accounts, litigation retainers, settlement proceeds, or disbursement funds. EMIs may only be considered for ancillary operating expenses, and even then with caution because the core treasury architecture of a cross-border litigation firm must remain bank-anchored in New Zealand.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The AML/CFT Act 2009 does not absolutely mandate physical branch attendance provided the bank can complete robust remote identity verification using biometric passports, liveness detection, and digital ID. In practice, however, for non-resident directors of a litigation firm opening a solicitors' trust account and capital escrow account, most New Zealand Tier 1 banks require either an in-branch interview at a New Zealand branch or a secure video interview with a relationship manager followed by certified hard-copy identity documents and notarised corporate resolutions. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for trust accounts because the bank must independently verify the statutory directors and the source of client funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: the litigation firm is backed by an overseas discretionary trust or holding company, making the ultimate beneficial owner unclear for the bank's customer due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full corporate org chart; trust deed and letter of wishes; register of beneficial owners; Companies Office certificate and NZBN extract; board resolution authorising account opening; passport copies and proof of residential address for every natural-person controller; signed UBO declaration; and a formal tax or legal opinion on the trust and the source of wealth of each effective owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound retainer or litigation-funding transfer from an opaque or higher-risk jurisdiction without an evidentiary link to the engagement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide 12 months of sending-entity bank statements; executed litigation funding agreement; signed retainer or engagement letter; itemised pro-forma invoice; sworn affidavit from the director or trustee explaining source of funds and source of wealth; forensic accountant report where funds originate from prior settlements or family wealth; and written confirmation that no sanctioned jurisdiction is involved in the payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursement of litigation proceeds to non-client third parties such as adverse parties, foreign counsel, expert witnesses, or overseas public bodies with insufficient commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the settlement agreement or arbitral award; applicable court order; costs breakdown and bill of costs; signed disbursement schedule; beneficiary KYC including legal entity name, jurisdiction, address, and bank account details; counsel undertakings; and enhanced due diligence on the beneficiary's bank if the receiving jurisdiction is considered high-risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of economic substance: the NZ Limited company appears to be a shell with only a registered office and no staff or physical presence in New Zealand.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide registered office or tenancy agreement; payroll records and employment agreements for the litigation team; GST and IRD registration documents; professional indemnity insurance certificate; AML/CFT compliance programme; firm organisational chart with director and staff biographies; New Zealand Law Society licensing or registration status; and, if useful, dated photographs of the physical premises.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound equity or retainer payments by SWIFT MT103 to the New Zealand bank account. For equity capital, instruct the sending bank to classify the credit as an equity injection into a New Zealand professional services company and use the appropriate balance-of-payments/ITRS purpose code provided by the receiving relationship manager; for legal fees and retainers, use a service-related purpose code such as legal services or professional advisory fees in SWIFT field 70. The receiving bank will require a statutory declaration, accountant's capital verification certificate, and board resolution if the injection is recorded for Companies Office or tax purposes. For FX conversion, execute the spot transaction with the New Zealand bank at the onshore NZD rate, and ensure the SWIFT reference contains the RBNZ balance-of-payments reporting code before settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For NZD-denominated local payments, use the ESAS high-value clearing system via the bank. For cross-border disbursements of settlement proceeds, witness fees, foreign counsel costs, or court-mandated payments, use SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details and a reference to the judgment or settlement agreement. MT202 COV may be used for interbank transfers where the beneficiary is a bank. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are generally not the standard clearing rails for litigation service fees, but they may be acceptable in ancillary trade-dispute settlements where a standby letter of credit is lodged as security or a documentary collection is used to release shipping documents under a court-approved arrangement. All disbursements from the IOLTA-style trust account must be supported by a written instruction, approved costs schedule, and client authority.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a New Zealand registered bank for firm future payment dates under verified litigation settlement or funding obligations.
Cross-currency swaps to align foreign-currency litigation assets with NZD operating liabilities, provided the notional is strictly tied to documented treasury exposure.
Vanilla FX options to hedge uncertain settlement amounts or contingent legal fees, without leveraged structures.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for hedging residual exposure to non-convertible currencies encountered in asset-tracing or enforcement matters; NZD/USD NDFs are not needed because the New Zealand dollar is fully deliverable onshore.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Companies Act 1993
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Registrar of Companies (Companies Office, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of incorporation for first return; thereafter on or before the company's annual return date, which is the anniversary of incorporation; filing is permitted one month before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of NZD 50 (approx USD 33); if the return is still not filed after the Registrar's 20-working-day statutory removal notice, the company is administratively struck off and dissolved, and the company's assets vest in the Crown

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Auditor's Report, when compulsory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Registrar of Companies (Companies Office, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance date for a compulsory filer; for the standard 31 March balance date, on or before 30 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing exposes the company and directors to Financial Reporting Act 2013 enforcement, compliance orders, financial penalties, and further action by the Financial Markets Authority, including public registration of default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (IRD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due by 7 July after balance date, unless Inland Revenue grants an extension of time
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250, then NZD 50 per month up to NZD 500; use-of-money interest accrues on any unpaid tax; continued default can result in IRD prosecution and director assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Annual Schedule (IR348) if any employees are engaged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (IRD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 20 June following the 31 March tax year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Employer penalties of NZD 250 per schedule, monthly incremental late-filing penalties, unpaid PAYE can become a personal liability for directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Solicitor's Trust Account (client funds / IOLTA-equivalent) Independent Audit and Accountant's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Law Society under the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 trust account regulations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: As required by New Zealand Law Society trust account audit rules; for a 31 March balance date, the complete trust account audit report is due on or before 30 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A qualified, qualified-with-emphasis or adverse trust account report is a major regulatory default; sanctions include conditions on or removal of the practising certificate, random inspection, Law Society investigation, intervention, compensation fund claim, and disciplinary charges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Programme Review and Compliance Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Internal Affairs of New Zealand (AML/CFT supervisor for legal practitioners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than 6 months after the balance date; the written AML/CFT programme must be reviewed and, where required, independently audited each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Maintaining an ineffective or unaudited AML/CFT programme is an offence; DIA may issue infringement notices, require remedial action, impose civil penalties up to NZD 2 million per contravention, and officers may face imprisonment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory certified CPA audit is mandatory for an NZ Limited company when: (a) it is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (e.g. public issuance of financial products, regulated managed investment or trust funds); (b) it is an overseas-owned company or large company required to file audited financial statements under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; (c) it satisfies at least two of the quantitative large-company tests: total consolidated assets greater than NZD 60,000,000; annual consolidated revenue greater than NZD 30,000,000; or 100 or more full-time-equivalent employees. In addition, a law firm maintaining client/IOLTA trust money is subject to a separate annual trust account audit by an independent licensed accountant in all cases, and shareholders holding 5% or more of voting rights can requisition a statutory audit by notice before the auditor appointment window
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ GAAP as adopted by the New Zealand External Reporting Board. For-profit entities apply New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS); eligible entities may apply the NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime; small private entities that are not filing entities maintain tax and financial records sufficient to prepare special purpose reports where applicable; audits must be performed under New Zealand Auditing Standards (NZ ISA)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not have a separate UBO filing form; the statutory annual confirmation is the annual return, which records current shareholders, directors, addresses and officers. Any change of directors, registered office or registered residential details must be notified to the Companies Office within 20 working days. Incoming share transfers must be posted to the company's own statutory share register and to the member roll promptly, and the next annual return must reflect the updated shareholding. New Zealand law does not create a 30-day UBO reporting window; the operative filing rule is the 20-working-day Companies Register notification rule, supplemented by AML/CFT beneficial-owner CDD records at the law-firm level
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges / register of mortgages and modifications
Minute Book containing directors' and shareholders' resolutions and consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 320 - USD 1,000 per annum for registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - USD 18,500 per annum for a certified statutory or trust account audit; higher for cross-border consolidated FMC reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays apply. A full imputation system applies to resident shareholders. Eligible R&D expenditure may qualify for the 15% R&D Tax Incentive. There is no separate capital gains tax. Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test; the machine-readable value 0 denotes indefinite carry-forward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through myIR or approved tax software using the Inland Revenue gateway.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax is generally payable in three instalments during the income year for companies with residual income tax over NZD 5,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, self-filers must file by 7 July following the balance date. Tax agents with an extension of time must file by 31 March of the following income year. For non-standard balance dates, the self-filer deadline is the 7th day of the 4th month after balance date, unless an alternative filing date is granted by Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, IRD number, registered office, postal address, and electronic contact details of the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-resident status and country of tax residence. If non-resident controlled, attach a schedule of directors, ultimate shareholders, and any applicable treaty residence claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period covered by the return, such as 1 April to 31 March, including short-period dates for newly incorporated or deregistered companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the New Zealand return period. A NZ tax resident company must report worldwide income; a non-resident company reports only New Zealand-source income and income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income from all sources, including legal fees, litigation funding recoveries, settlement proceeds, and any taxable business receipts, excluding exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income derived from New Zealand sources or through a New Zealand permanent establishment. Cross-border commercial litigation management fees earned offshore and not attributable to a NZ PE are excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: New Zealand-sourced interest, dividends, royalties, and other investment income, with resident withholding tax or non-resident withholding tax credits separately itemised.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross New Zealand-sourced investment income. Attach Tax Residency Certificates where treaty-reduced withholding rates have been applied and claim the credits withheld at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses incurred in deriving assessable income, including staff costs, premises, professional indemnity insurance, bank charges, and IOLTA trust account administration costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses actually incurred by the New Zealand branch or company are deductible. Head-office overhead allocations must be arm's length and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income less deductible expenses, before loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the New Zealand PE net profit under New Zealand tax law. Non-allowable deductions, notional internal charges, and foreign taxes are excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years and current-year group loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss offset is available only if the 49% shareholder continuity test is satisfied. Non-resident companies may offset losses only against New Zealand-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit after deduction of available loss offsets; taxable income is assessed at the 28% corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with no New Zealand permanent establishment and no New Zealand-source income should record zero taxable income. Treaty-protected income must be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax at 28%, reduced by imputation credits, RWT credits, provisional tax paid, and foreign tax credits, resulting in residual tax payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imputation credits are not refundable to non-resident shareholders. Any apparent refund arising from imputation credits must be reviewed for non-resident withholding tax consequences.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per month or part-month, capped at NZD 500, applies to each overdue IR4. Late payment penalties accrue at 1% of unpaid tax from the day after the due date, an additional 4% after seven days, and further monthly penalty charges until paid. Use-of-money interest is also charged on unpaid tax. Persistent non-filing may trigger default assessments and revocation of tax agent concessions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory non-resident withholding tax rate on dividends is 30%. A fully imputed dividend paid to an Australian resident may attract a 0% rate under the New Zealand-Australia DTA. Other applicable DTA rates generally range from 5% for substantial shareholdings to 15% for portfolio investors.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the New Zealand payer with a current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the home-jurisdiction tax authority. The payer applies the reduced DTA rate and retains the certificate with the dividend documentation. For uncertain arrangements, the payer or payee may seek a binding ruling from Inland Revenue under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Treaty relief is available only to the beneficial owner, not to conduit entities or nominees.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT for interest is 15% and for royalties is 15%. Under most New Zealand DTAs, interest is reduced to 10% and royalties to 5%-10%, with certain categories of government interest exempt. An Approved Issuer Levy of 2% may be paid instead of NRWT on interest to an unassociated non-resident lender where the borrower is an approved issuer and the loan is registered with Inland Revenue; AIL is not available for associated-party loans or royalty payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 aggregate cross-border associated-party transactions per income year triggers the expectation of contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation. Below this threshold, documentation is not statutorily mandatory but is strongly recommended to support arm's length pricing and penalty relief.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations code of the offshore-hub type. However, the New Zealand tax residence definition, the general anti-avoidance rule, CFC rules, and the licensing and conduct requirements of the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 impose a real economic substance test. A New Zealand litigation company must maintain physical premises, staff, governance, client files, and active decision-making functions in New Zealand. An entity lacking commercial substance may be disregarded, treated as tax transparent, denied treaty benefits, or recharacterised under Part G of the Income Tax Act 2007.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting New Zealand-sourced legal fee income, manufacturing false expense invoices, destroying books and records, or concealing offshore beneficial ownership of the litigation company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalty up to 150% of the tax shortfall under section 141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994. Criminal conviction under section 143A carries imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines up to NZD 50,000 for individuals, or up to NZD 250,000 for a body corporate. Inland Revenue may also issue amended assessments, impose late payment penalties, and charge use-of-money interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise or participate in evasion may be prosecuted as parties to the offending. The corporate veil is pierced in cases of fraud; courts may order restitution of diverted assets, disqualify directors for up to 10 years under the Companies Act 1994, and impose asset freezing orders and bail conditions that effectively restrict international travel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-arm's length management fees, inflated interest, or excessive royalties to an offshore associate; failing to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million; or maintaining a debt-to-asset ratio above 60% for non-resident controlled entities without commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may reprice transactions, deny interest deductions, and recharacterise excessive debt as equity under the transfer pricing and thin capitalisation rules. Shortfall penalties range from 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for an unacceptable tax position, up to 150% for evasion. Interest deductions on excessive non-resident debt may be wholly or partially disallowed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation may be personally liable for penalties as parties to tax avoidance. If the arrangement is a sham, the corporate veil is pierced and directors may be required to make restitution. Serious cases are referred to criminal prosecution, and departing directors may be subject to travel bans while under investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Abuse / Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a New Zealand company with no physical office, no employees, no New Zealand bank account, and no client-facing activity to access the New Zealand tax treaty network, manufacture artificial tax losses, or disguise the true commercial principal in cross-border litigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1 and specific anti-avoidance provisions in Part G allow the Commissioner to cancel tax benefits, reconstruct the arrangement, and deny DTA benefits under the principal purpose test. Shortfall penalties up to 100% for abusive tax positions may apply, and loss offsets are denied unless the 49% shareholder continuity test is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for company tax liabilities where the shell company is used as an instrument of fraud. Liability may also arise for fraudulent trading under the Companies Act 1994. Courts may issue civil recovery orders and travel restrictions pending investigation or prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and IOLTA Trust Account Misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The commercial litigation firm fails to maintain an AML/CFT compliance programme, fails to conduct customer due diligence, or uses the IOLTA trust account to launder settlement proceeds, move client funds without a legitimate underlying matter, or circumvent foreign exchange controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 up to NZD 2 million for a reporting entity. Criminal liability for money laundering under the Crimes Act 1961 carries imprisonment up to 7 years. Professional discipline includes fine, suspension, or strike-off under the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006, together with compensation orders from the Lawyers Fidelity Fund.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Principals and directors who knowingly permit misuse of trust money are personally liable to repay the shortfall. The corporate veil will be pierced for theft by a person in a special relationship. Asset restraint orders and forfeiture proceedings may be brought under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009, and bail conditions may include surrender of passports, effectively imposing travel bans.
